title: Trump Offers White House Press Secretary Job to UFC CEO Dana White
snippet: President Donald Trump has publicly extended an offer to Ultimate Fighting Championship CEO Dana White to serve as the next White House press secretary, suggesting the fight executive bring top mixed martial artists to the briefing room.
content:
WASHINGTON — In an unprecedented proposal that blurs the lines between political communications and combat sports, President Donald Trump announced Saturday that he has offered the role of White House press secretary to UFC Chief Executive Dana White.

Taking to his Truth Social platform, Trump praised the 57-year-old fight promoter, describing him as a "violent Fighter and Warrior" capable of taking on the Washington press corps.

"I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White... has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States," Trump wrote. In characteristic style, the president suggested White assemble a powerhouse squad of elite fighters to assist him at the podium, explicitly naming UFC stars Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and "Kayla Harris" — an apparent misspelling of Olympic gold medalist and UFC champion Kayla Harrison.

"We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!" Trump added.

While White has not issued a formal public statement regarding the offer, he stoked speculation by sharing a screenshot of Trump’s post on his Instagram story alongside an image of himself standing behind the White House press briefing room podium with the caption, "On to the next chapter."

A Long-Standing Partnership

The offer marks the latest chapter in a quarter-century relationship between the business mogul and the fight executive. Their bond dates back to 2001, when Trump hosted UFC 30 at his Trump Taj Mahal casino in Atlantic City, New Jersey, during a period when mixed martial arts was banned in most U.S. states.

White has frequently repaid that early support, campaigning prominently for Trump during all three of his presidential runs and speaking on his behalf at the Republican National Conventions in 2016, 2020, and 2024. The partnership reached a high mark earlier this summer when the White House hosted "UFC Freedom 250" on the South Lawn, solidifying White's position within the president's inner circle.

Turmoil at the Press Podium

The White House press secretary position has been vacant for just over two weeks following the abrupt resignation of Katie Zacharia. Zacharia stepped down after five turbulent days in the role, which began with a brief five-minute initial briefing and ended amid intense scrutiny over her professional background.

Zacharia had originally replaced Karoline Leavitt, who departed the administration in August for maternity leave following the birth of her second child. In the interim, senior administration officials including Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio have occasionally filled in at the press briefing room lectern.

Whether White intends to accept the position or remain at the helm of the multi-billion-dollar combat sports enterprise remains unclear. However, his potential appointment would signal a dramatically confrontational pivot in the administration's media strategy.
